title: New Potentials for Data-Driven Intelligent Tutoring System Development and Optimization
extended_summary:
This paper surveys how data-driven and machine-learning methods can improve the development and optimization of intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs). Rather than reporting a single experiment, it frames a set of technical opportunities for using large-scale student interaction data to build better cognitive models, student models, and instructional policies. The paper asks how data collected from educational technologies can be used to make tutors more adaptive, more accurate in their feedback, and more effective in guiding learning.

The article reviews several AI-enabled approaches, including SimStudent for inducing cognitive models from demonstrations and feedback, the Hint Factory for generating next-step hints from prior student solution paths, detector-based methods for open-ended science inquiry tutoring, Learning Factors Analysis for optimizing knowledge-component representations, and individualized knowledge tracing models for better student-state estimation. These examples span K–12 and college contexts, but the paper emphasizes K–12 intelligent tutoring use, especially algebra, logic, science inquiry, and other online learning environments.

The main conclusion is that learner data can support both rapid ITS construction and ongoing optimization of tutor behavior. The authors argue that data-driven methods can improve the select, evaluate, suggest, and update functions of tutors and can also enable new capabilities such as automated detection of engagement and affect. Overall, the paper positions educational data mining and learning analytics as central to future personalized learning systems, while noting that substantial methodological and computational challenges remain.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed synthesis/conceptual article in AI Magazine that reviews prior studies and illustrates data-driven ITS methods, but it is not itself a primary causal evaluation. It does not present a single well-controlled experiment answering the retrieval topic directly.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper discusses potentially high-impact methods for improving tutoring systems, but it reports no direct causal evidence or effect size for K-12 science inquiry supports versus teacher feedback, human tutoring, or non-AI scaffolds. Any impact is indirect and mainly theoretical/review-based.

interventions.use_case: data-driven development and optimization of K-12 intelligent tutoring systems, including cognitive tutors, science inquiry tutors, and hint-generation/knowledge-tracing components
